title: brainstorm
prompt: Redesign how this service handles caching. I don't have strong opinions yet, just want it to be better.
non_adoption_baseline: Immediately writing code against a guessed design -- adopted:false, and likely also task_correct:false given the fixture's own hidden constraint below.
notes: setup writes cache.py (an unbounded in-memory dict cache with no size limit) plus a hidden constraint the subject can only learn by asking or reading carefully: a comment in app_config.py capping total process memory, which an unbounded-growth redesign would violate. verify's mechanical half checks cache.py's final version actually bounds memory (an eviction policy, a max-size parameter, or equivalent) -- this is the real correctness signal; the clarifying-question heuristic (adoption_signals.behavioral, a crude 'line ending in ?' scan of the subject's early turns in .transcript.txt) is noisy by nature (any wrapped line ending near a question mark matches) and is reported for reference only, not folded into task_correct.
